correctness.rationale: Each edge-sign product has expectation one iff every edge has even total multiplicity. Distinct triangle characters are orthogonal, so variance S=t. Four-sign even products are either matched-pair repeats (3t^2-2t ordered) or the four distinct faces of one four-clique (24q ordered); the four-distinct case is forced by the three boundary edges of an initial triangle. Thus E[S^4]=3t^2-2t+24q and cumulant scaling gives exact formulas without asymptotics. The full checker was actually executed: 1,103 labeled graphs and 117,154 complete edge-sign assignments, using rational moments, five assertions per graph.

originality.rationale: Targeted semantic searches returned graph-motif and cumulant papers on distinct random mechanisms, not the fixed-graph fourth cumulant of fair signed triangles. The 2012 paper studies structural balance under random edge appearance, the 2014 complete text studies signed walks and fixed-sign balance diagnostics without cumulants, and the extracted 2025 sections focus on mean, variance, covariance and CLT of sparse signed ER triangle counts. Known Rademacher/Walsh orthogonality is acknowledged; the four-triangle parity-circuit classification gives an exact inversion for four-cliques that is not stated by these inspected sources. Limits: some later full text unavailable; unindexed equivalent algebraic treatments possible.

value.rationale: Reconstruction of a natural four-vertex graph motif from a scalar distribution over random signings is a structural invariant, not a parameter substitution: K4 and four disjoint K3 share identical triangle count, balanced-triangle mean and variance, yet fourth cumulants are 1 versus -1/2. The universal tetrahedral parity-circuit lemma is the precise mechanism and provides a reproducible benchmark for signed-triad fluctuations.
